text: Pronouncing syllables, investigating words, memorizing plays, or making rules for the scansion of poetry,—what is there in all this that rids one of fear, roots out desire, or bridles the passions?
plain: Knowing a lot of trivia does nothing about your fear or your cravings. Study what changes you.

text: The mathematician teaches me how I may lose none of my boundaries; I, however, seek to learn how to lose them all with a light heart.
plain: Learn to lose things without it wrecking you.

text: You are showing me what the doleful keys are; show me rather how, in the midst of adversity, I may keep from uttering a doleful note.
plain: Skip the theory. Teach me how to stay steady when things go bad.

text: You know what a straight line is; but how does it benefit you if you do not know what is straight in this life of ours?
plain: Smart about everything except how to live is not smart.

text: I, for my part, do not know what is to be, but I do know what may come to be. I shall have no misgivings in this matter; I await the future in its entirety; and if there is any abatement in its severity, I make the most of it.
plain: You can't know what's coming, but you can be ready for all of it. Take any mercy as a bonus.

text: I am ready for favourable events in every case, but I am prepared for evil.
plain: Hope for the good, plan for the bad.

text: Bravery is a scorner of things which inspire fear; it looks down upon, challenges, and crushes the powers of terror and all that would drive our freedom under the yoke.
plain: Courage means staring down what scares you until it loses its hold.

text: Temperance knows that the best measure of the appetites is not what you want to take, but what you ought to take.
plain: Measure yourself by what you should have, not what you want.

text: Let all other things be driven out, and let the breast be emptied to receive virtue.
plain: Clear out the clutter to make room for what matters.

text: Come now, do not tell me that life is long!
plain: Life is short. Stop spending it on junk.

text: Study, not in order to add anything to your knowledge, but to make your knowledge better.
plain: Learn to improve how you live, not to pile up facts.

text: Medicine begins to do good at the time when a touch makes the diseased body tingle with pain.
plain: The truth stings because it's starting to work.

text: At times you should allow words other than compliments to reach your ears, and because as individuals you are unwilling to hear the truth, hear it collectively.
plain: Let people tell you what you don't want to hear.

text: What profit to you are your many bed-chambers? You sleep in one.
plain: You can only use so much. The rest is for show.

text: Poor wretches, do you not know that your appetites are bigger than your bellies?
plain: You want far more than you can ever enjoy.

text: An estate which held a nation is too narrow for a single lord.
plain: Greed never reaches a point where it feels like enough.

text: Who can doubt, my dear Lucilius, that life is the gift of the immortal gods, but that living well is the gift of philosophy?
plain: Being alive is given. Living well you have to learn.

text: A thatched roof once covered free men; under marble and gold dwells slavery.
plain: The more luxury you need, the less free you are.

text: Fool that I am, to have been carrying superfluous baggage all this time!
plain: Look at what you carry around and drop whatever you don't need.

text: The things that are indispensable require no elaborate pains for their acquisition; it is only the luxuries that call for labour.
plain: What you truly need is cheap. The hard grind is for extras.

text: All things were ready for us at our birth; it is we that have made everything difficult for ourselves, through our disdain for what is easy.
plain: Most of the struggle is self-made by refusing the simple route.

text: It was avarice that introduced poverty and, by craving much, lost all.
plain: Wanting everything is how people end up with nothing.

text: Care vexes us in our purple, and routs us from our beds with the sharpest of goads; but how soft was the sleep the hard earth bestowed upon the men of that day!
plain: Comfort brings worry. People on hard beds slept better.

text: Virtue is not vouchsafed to a soul unless that soul has been trained and taught, and by unremitting practice brought to perfection.
plain: Being good is a skill. It takes daily reps.

text: Strangeness adds to the weight of calamities, and every mortal feels the greater pain as a result of that which also brings surprise.
plain: Surprise makes bad news hit harder. Expect the hit and it weighs less.

text: Our minds should be sent forward in advance to meet all problems, and we should consider, not what is wont to happen, but what can happen.
plain: Rehearse the worst case before it shows up.

text: No time is exempt; in the midst of our very pleasures there spring up causes of suffering.
plain: Good times don't protect you. Stay ready.

text: Nothing, whether public or private, is stable; the destinies of men, no less than those of cities, are in a whirl.
plain: Nothing stays put. Plan for change.

text: It would be some consolation for the feebleness of our selves and our works, if all things should perish as slowly as they come into being; but as it is, increases are of sluggish growth, but the way to ruin is rapid.
plain: Building is slow and falling is fast, so guard what you build.

text: Let us rise, therefore, to confront the operations of Fortune, and whatever happens, let us have the assurance that it is not so great as rumour advertises it to be.
plain: Whatever hits you is never as big as the hype around it.

text: It would be tedious to recount all the ways by which fate may come; but this one thing I know: all the works of mortal man have been doomed to mortality, and in the midst of things which have been destined to die, we live!
plain: Everything made dies. We live anyway, so live fully.

text: Oftentimes a reverse has but made room for more prosperous fortune. Many structures have fallen only to rise to a greater height.
plain: A loss can clear the ground for something bigger.

text: We are unequal at birth, but are equal in death.
plain: Death levels everyone, rich or poor.

text: You must suffer pain, and thirst, and hunger, and old age too, if a longer stay among men shall be granted you; you must be sick, and you must suffer loss and death.
plain: Hardship comes with being alive. Don't be shocked by it.

text: What madness it is to be afraid of disrepute in the judgment of the disreputable!
plain: Why fear the opinion of people you don't respect?

text: For me the talk of ignorant men is like the rumblings which issue from the belly.
plain: Noise from fools is just noise.

text: I cannot give anything easier to any man, but whoever wishes will make things easier for himself.
plain: Life won't get softer. Your attitude can.

text: What is the happy life? It is peace of mind, and lasting tranquillity.
plain: Happiness is a calm mind that lasts.

text: That man, I declare, is happy whom nothing makes less strong than he is; he keeps to the heights, leaning upon none but himself; for one who sustains himself by any prop may fall.
plain: Lean on yourself. Anything else you depend on can give way.

text: The scabbard does not make the sword good or bad.
plain: Packaging doesn't change what you are.

text: Disasters, therefore, and losses, and wrongs, have only the same power over virtue that a cloud has over the sun.
plain: Bad luck can dim you but can't put you out.

text: If virtue only stands her ground, she cannot be driven from the field; she must either conquer or be conquered.
plain: Hold your ground and you can't be pushed off it.

text: The soul, I affirm, knows that riches are stored elsewhere than in men’s heaped-up treasure-houses; that it is the soul, and not the strong-box, which should be filled.
plain: Fill yourself up, not the vault.

text: We should strive, not to live long, but to live rightly; for to achieve long life you have need of Fate only, but for right living you need the soul.
plain: Length of life is luck. Quality is up to you.

text: Pray, let us see to it, my dear Lucilius, that our lives, like jewels of great price, be noteworthy not because of their width but because of their weight. Let us measure them by their performance, not by their duration.
plain: Judge a life by what it did, not how long it ran.

text: Just as one of small stature can be a perfect man, so a life of small compass can be a perfect life.
plain: A short life can still be complete.

text: How long I am to exist is not mine to decide, but how long I shall go on existing in my present way is in my own control.
plain: You can't pick your lifespan. You can pick how you live.

text: This is the only thing you have the right to require of me,—that I shall cease to measure out an inglorious age as it were in darkness, and devote myself to living instead of being carried along past life.
plain: Stop drifting through the years. Actually live them.

text: And what, you ask, is the fullest span of life? It is living until you possess wisdom.
plain: A full life is one where you've learned how to live.

text: And anyhow, what does it matter for how long a time you avoid that which you cannot escape?
plain: Delaying the inevitable doesn't beat it.

text: We miss much that is set before our very eyes.
plain: A lot of what you need is already in front of you. You just miss it.

text: Buy not what you need, but what you must have. That which you do not need, is dear even at a farthing.
plain: Anything you don't need is expensive, even if it's cheap.

text: Fortune favours the brave, but the coward is foiled by his faint heart.
plain: Nerve gets rewarded. Fear gets you beat.

text: Nothing is more successful in bringing honourable influences to bear upon the mind, or in straightening out the wavering spirit that is prone to evil, than association with good men.
plain: Your circle shapes you more than willpower does.

text: Nobody confines his mistakes to himself; people sprinkle folly among their neighbours, and receive it from them in turn.
plain: Bad habits spread between people. Choose who you're around.

text: If you would wield a command that is profitable to yourself, and injurious to nobody, clear your own faults out of the way.
plain: Fix yourself before you try to lead.

text: You need never believe that a man can become happy through the unhappiness of another.
plain: Climbing over people never makes you happy.

text: Who puts on the purple robe for the sake of flaunting it in no man’s eyes? Who uses gold plate when he dines alone?
plain: Most flexing is for an audience.

text: You can make us cease to crave, if you only make us cease to display.
plain: Cut the audience and the wanting fades.

text: Ambition, luxury, and waywardness need a stage to act upon; you will cure all those ills if you seek retirement.
plain: Pull back from the crowd and the urges quiet down.

text: That which others think elevated, is to them a sheer precipice.
plain: What looks like a high position from below feels like a cliff edge to the person standing on it.

text: It is prosperity that takes away righteousness.
plain: Comfort makes people soft and careless.

text: We often want one thing and pray for another, not telling the truth even to the gods, while the gods either do not hearken, or else take pity on us.
plain: We aren't honest even with ourselves about what we want.

text: You need not wonder that diseases are beyond counting: count the cooks!
plain: Excess feeds the problem. Count the indulgences.

text: We are mad, not only individually, but nationally.
plain: The craziness isn't just personal. It's everywhere.

text: Deeds that would be punished by loss of life when committed in secret, are praised by us because uniformed generals have carried them out.
plain: People call it fine as long as the right people do it.

text: The same act may be either shameful or honourable: the purpose and the manner make all the difference.
plain: Same action, different intent, different worth.

text: Life without ideals is erratic: as soon as an ideal is to be set up, doctrines begin to be necessary.
plain: Without a guiding principle you zigzag. Pick one.

text: We must set before our eyes the goal of the Supreme Good, towards which we may strive, and to which all our acts and words may have reference—just as sailors must guide their course according to a certain star.
plain: Pick a north star and steer by it.

text: I am sure you will admit that there is nothing more shameful than uncertain and wavering conduct, than the habit of timorous retreat.
plain: Flip-flopping and backing off is the real disgrace.

text: Would you win over the gods? Then be a good man. Whoever imitates them, is worshipping them sufficiently.
plain: Want to honor what is higher than you? Just be a good person.

text: What a little thing it is not to harm one whom you ought to help!
plain: Not hurting people is the bare minimum.

text: Our relations with one another are like a stone arch, which would collapse if the stones did not mutually support each other, and which is upheld in this very way.
plain: People hold each other up or everyone falls.

text: Let us banish rumour and set a value upon each thing, asking what it is and not what it is called.
plain: Judge things by what they are, not their reputation.

text: Peace of mind is enjoyed only by those who have attained a fixed and unchanging standard of judgment; the rest of mankind continually ebb and flow in their decisions, floating in a condition where they alternately reject things and seek them.
plain: Calm comes from standards that don't shift with every mood.

text: If you would always desire the same things, you must desire the truth.
plain: Chase what's true and your wants stop flipping.
